group: Energy Company Leadership and Market Entrants

customers.name: Energy Company Director
customers.description: COO, CFO or managing director of an energy supplier, BRP or portfolio operator in the Netherlands, Belgium, Spain or Portugal: from a 40,000-connection regional supplier or a cooperative such as Pure Energie to a national player such as Eneco, Essent, Vattenfall or Engie, or a trader and portfolio operator such as Axpo or EBN. Signs the platform subscription and the managed-service contracts, decides which suites (Supplier, Balancing & Shipping, Trade & Portfolio) and which market roles are run in-house or outsourced, sponsors the consolidation of heritage systems (Ecedo, Energy21 EBASE, Jules, Gridhub, Nemon, home-grown billing) onto one platform, and answers personally to shareholders, the ACM or CNMC, TenneT and the auditors. Judges the platform on gross margin per connection, cost to serve, straight-through billing, imbalance cost, time to market for propositions and the risk of a migration going wrong in front of hundreds of thousands of customers.
careAbout: Gross margin per connection in a retail market where the ACM tariff rules, price caps and switching rates squeeze the spread between sourcing cost and the customer price
Cost to serve per connection: every manual correction, estimated bill, rejected switch or avoidable call is a direct hit on a margin of a few euros per month
Never being the supplier that misses a market change: Allocation 2.0 reconciliation, the 15-minute day-ahead market, aFRR changes, the net-metering phase-out or a CNMC settlement rule
Launching propositions in weeks rather than eighteen months, because a dynamic, EV or battery product that lands late is margin a competitor books
One operational backbone from proposition to cash and settlement instead of five heritage products, spreadsheets and a third-party BRP that each hold a piece of the truth
A migration or acquisition that does not disrupt billing, market communication or nominations for a single day
winsThem: A 15-minute view of margin, position and cost per segment that the board can act on instead of a month-end reconstruction
Straight-through billing and switching that let the business grow connections without growing the back office
Market and regulatory changes shipped by the vendor to every tenant before the go-live date, with a parallel run to prove it
A credible migration plan with tooling, references and support-until-decommission terms that removes consolidation risk from the board agenda
The option to buy balance responsibility, market entry or licensing as a managed service with a guaranteed cycle rather than hiring scarce specialists
theirFear: A billing or market-communication failure after a migration that produces wrong invoices for hundreds of thousands of customers and a regulator inquiry
Imbalance or sourcing cost that blows through the budget in a volatile quarter because positions were only visible after the fact
Being locked into a vendor whose roadmap, ownership or country coverage no longer matches a buy-and-build strategy

jobsToBeDone.name: Grow margin per connection while cutting cost to serve
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Raise the gross margin the company earns on every household, business and industrial connection while lowering the operational cost of onboarding, billing, collecting and serving that connection, by running order-to-cash straight through, moving customers to self-service, launching margin-accretive propositions quickly and keeping sourcing and imbalance cost under control.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Gross margin per connection rises year over year while cost to serve falls; the company adds connections and propositions without adding back-office or trading headcount, and the board sees margin per segment every 15 minutes instead of at month end.

steps.step: See margin, cost and position per segment
steps.description: Replace the month-end reconstruction in spreadsheets with a live view of sourcing cost, imbalance cost, allocated volumes, billed revenue and margin per segment (households, SME, industrial, producers) so that decisions about pricing, hedging and cost programmes rest on the same numbers as settlement.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Tracks the sourced cost, hedge coverage and margin of the portfolio per segment against the prices sold to customers.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Delivers allocated and reconciled volumes and imbalance settlement per 15 minutes, the volume side of the margin calculation.

steps.step: Run order-to-cash straight through
steps.description: Take intake, switching, contract creation, meter data, billing runs, VAT, guarantees of origin, payments and dunning through one flow with exceptions handled by workflow rather than by administrators re-keying data, so that a connection costs a few euros a year to operate rather than tens.

streamsNeeded.name: Onboard and Switch Customers
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Automates intake, credit check, contract creation and the EDSN or SIPS switch so that new connections activate without manual handling.

streamsNeeded.name: Bill and Reconcile Customers
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Runs billing from validated volumes and contracts with corrections and exceptions as the measured minority.

streamsNeeded.name: Collect Payments and Manage Debtors
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Matches direct debits and payments automatically and runs dunning and payment plans without a debtor team growing with the base.

steps.step: Move customers to self-service on billing data
steps.description: Open the white-label portal and app so that invoices, consumption, meter readings, tariff changes, payment changes and disputes happen on the same data as billing and settlement, which removes the contacts and the back-office corrections that self-service on a copy of the data creates.

streamsNeeded.name: Serve Customers Through Portal and Care
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the branded portal and app plus case management that turn avoidable contacts into completed self-service tasks.

steps.step: Launch margin-accretive propositions in weeks
steps.description: Let the commercial team configure dynamic, time-of-use, EV, battery, capacity-linked and bundled propositions with their pricing logic and channels in the low-code builder and take them live within weeks, so that margin opportunities such as the 15-minute day-ahead market or the net-metering phase-out are captured before competitors land.

streamsNeeded.name: Launch Energy Propositions and Tariffs
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Turns a proposition idea into a configured, billable product in weeks instead of an IT project.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Prices each proposition cost-plus from the actual portfolio cost and price curves so that volume growth is margin growth.

steps.step: Bring sourcing and imbalance cost under control
steps.description: Improve day-ahead, intraday and ex-post forecasts, steer intraday through ETPA and flexible assets, and decide whether balance responsibility stays in-house or moves to BRP as a Service, so that imbalance cost per MWh stops being the largest unexplained line in the margin bridge.

streamsNeeded.name: Forecast and Nominate the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Improves forecast accuracy and nomination timeliness, the two levers behind imbalance cost.

streamsNeeded.name: Steer Intraday and Optimise Imbalance
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Reduces imbalance cost through intraday trading and flex steering, in-house or as a managed guaranteed cycle.

steps.step: Decide where the freed margin and capacity go
steps.description: Review gross margin per connection, cost to serve and headcount per process quarterly on the operational dashboard, compare segments and propositions, and choose between price competitiveness, a new segment, a second country or an acquisition.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Shows margin per segment and proposition over time so that the board sees the effect of each pricing, automation and self-service step.

streamsNeeded.name: Enter and Operate in a New Energy Market
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the market-entry scan and operating-model options when the freed capacity is pointed at a new country.

jobsToBeDone.name: Stay compliant with every market and regulatory change
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Keep the company's propositions, market communication, billing, settlement and reporting compliant with every change the ACM, CNMC, TenneT, EDSN, the gas TSOs, OMIE and the legislator introduce, from Allocation 2.0 reconciliation and the 15-minute day-ahead market to tariff-transparency rules, the net-metering phase-out and Iberian settlement changes, without a compliance programme per change.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Every market change is live on its go-live date across every brand and tenant with a parallel run behind it; regulatory reports go out on time; compliance incidents and regulator findings approach zero; the director stops being surprised by a change six weeks before it lands.

steps.step: Track upcoming market and regulatory changes
steps.description: Maintain one calendar of market and regulatory changes across electricity and gas, the Netherlands and Iberia: EDSN release cycles, TenneT MMC-Hub tranches, day-ahead and aFRR market design changes, ACM tariff and consumer-protection rules, the 2027 net-metering phase-out, CNMC settlement and switching-file changes.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Carries the BRP compliance calendar and the settlement rule versions per market that the company is bound to.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate Market Communication and External Systems
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Tracks EDSN, C-AR, TenneT, ETPA, OMIE and REE/SIPS message-format and connector releases per date.

steps.step: Assess impact on propositions, billing and settlement
steps.description: For each change, determine which propositions, tariffs, invoice lines, allocation rules, nominations and reports are affected and what customers must be told, so that the commercial, billing and balancing teams work from one impact analysis instead of three.

streamsNeeded.name: Launch Energy Propositions and Tariffs
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Shows which live propositions, tariffs and pricing rules the change touches and lets them be versioned per go-live date.

streamsNeeded.name: Bill and Reconcile Customers
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Identifies invoice lines, VAT and settlement logic that must change and the customers affected.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Assesses the effect on allocation, reconciliation and imbalance settlement per connection type.

steps.step: Let the vendor ship the change to every tenant
steps.description: Rely on the platform to implement the market-communication, allocation and settlement changes once and roll them out to every brand and tenant, so that the company pays for a subscription rather than for a change project per regulation.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate Market Communication and External Systems
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Delivers the updated EDSN, TenneT, OMIE and SIPS connectors and message formats to all tenants before the cut-over date.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Implements new allocation, reconciliation and settlement rules such as Allocation 2.0 tranche 3 platform-wide.

steps.step: Verify before go-live with a parallel run
steps.description: Run the changed billing, allocation and settlement logic in parallel on real data for a bounded set of connections, compare results and sign off, so that the go-live date is a non-event rather than a bet.

streamsNeeded.name: Collect and Validate Meter Data
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides validated volumes for the parallel run and flags where new interval or connection-type rules change the outcome.

streamsNeeded.name: Bill and Reconcile Customers
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Runs the shadow billing run and reconciles it against the current logic before the change goes live.

steps.step: Report to regulators, TSOs and the board
steps.description: Produce the ACM, CNMC, TenneT and BRP compliance reports and the customer disclosures each change requires, and show the board and the auditors that every change was live on time with evidence.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Generates BRP compliance and settlement reports with the audit trail behind each figure.

streamsNeeded.name: Serve Customers Through Portal and Care
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Sends the regulatory disclosures and tariff-change communications customers must receive, per brand and channel.

jobsToBeDone.name: Consolidate operations on one platform without disruption
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Move the company's brands, connections, contracts, meter data, market roles and portfolios from several heritage systems and outsourced services onto one platform, including the businesses it acquires, without a single missed billing run, rejected market message or late nomination, and decommission the old systems and their licence, hosting and specialist cost.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Every connection and portfolio runs on the target platform; heritage systems are switched off; migration incidents stay below the threshold agreed with the regulator; an acquired supplier or portfolio is absorbed within two quarters on the same tooling.

steps.step: Inventory heritage systems, roles and contracts
steps.description: List every system, interface, market role, external service and contract that touches the operation: the heritage billing package, the separate CRM, the pricing spreadsheets, the third-party BRP, the meter-data provider, the payment provider, the accounting system and the connectors between them, with their costs and end dates.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate Market Communication and External Systems
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Maps every existing connector and market-communication endpoint to the platform's certified connectors and open API.

steps.step: Sequence the migration by brand and segment
steps.description: Decide the order in which brands, customer segments, gas and electricity, and market roles move, starting with a bounded segment and ending with the largest, and agree freeze windows with billing, market communication and balancing so that no cut-over collides with an annual settlement run or a market change.

streamsNeeded.name: Onboard and Switch Customers
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Shows which intake and switching flows per brand and channel must be live before each migration wave.

streamsNeeded.name: Bill and Reconcile Customers
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Fixes billing-cycle constraints and annual-settlement windows that the migration sequence must respect.

steps.step: Migrate data and market roles onto the platform
steps.description: Load customers, connections, contracts, meter histories, open invoices, payment arrangements and portfolio structures with the migration tooling, re-point EDSN, C-AR, TenneT, OMIE and SIPS endpoints, and transfer or newly contract the BRP and shipping roles, with validation reports per wave.

streamsNeeded.name: Collect and Validate Meter Data
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Re-establishes meter-data collection and validation for migrated connections without gaps in interval history.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate Market Communication and External Systems
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Re-points market-communication and external-system connections to the platform per migration wave.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Transfers allocation and settlement history so that reconciliation and imbalance settlement continue seamlessly.

steps.step: Parallel-run billing, settlement and nominations
steps.description: For each wave run billing, allocation, settlement and nominations in both the heritage system and the platform for at least one full cycle, compare invoices, volumes and positions, fix the mapping differences and sign off before the heritage run is stopped.

streamsNeeded.name: Bill and Reconcile Customers
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Produces the shadow billing run and the invoice-level comparison against the heritage system.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Compares allocated and settled volumes and imbalance positions between the two systems for the parallel period.

steps.step: Decommission heritage systems and retrain teams
steps.description: Switch off the old systems and services, cancel the licences and hosting, and put billing, customer-service and balancing staff through academy training so that the new workflow, exception handling and dashboards are used as intended rather than reproduced in spreadsheets.

streamsNeeded.name: Enter and Operate in a New Energy Market
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Delivers implementation support and academy training that make the operating teams productive on the platform.

streamsNeeded.name: Serve Customers Through Portal and Care
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Moves customer-service cases and communication from the heritage tools to the platform's case management and portal.

steps.step: Absorb acquired suppliers and portfolios
steps.description: When the company buys a competitor's customer base or a producer portfolio, migrate its connections, contracts and market roles with the same tooling and playbook, put its customers on the same brand portal or a separate one, and integrate its balancing into the existing portfolio within two quarters.

streamsNeeded.name: Onboard and Switch Customers
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Processes the bulk supplier switch of an acquired customer base through market communication without individual re-contracting.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate Market Communication and External Systems
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Connects the acquired company's meter-data, payment and accounting systems during the transition and retires them afterwards.

customerJourneyStories.name: From five heritage systems to one supplier platform
customerJourneyStories.summary: The COO of a 350,000-connection Dutch supplier that runs billing on a heritage SaaS package, customer service on a separate CRM, pricing in spreadsheets and balance responsibility at a third-party BRP consolidates onto the platform: discovering the merged vendor through the Eneve rebrand and a peer at a Vereniging Energie-Nederland meeting, evaluating on a demo with the supplier's own connections and on migration and support terms, running a parallel billing and settlement cycle on one brand, and renewing on cost to serve.

stages.narrative: The Allocation 2.0 tranche 3 reconciliation and the 15-minute day-ahead market land in the same year, each requiring a change project in three different systems, while the annual settlement run produces a correction rate the auditors flag. The COO concludes that the company is paying five vendors and a BRP to keep pieces of one process alive and that the next market change will break it.

The June 2025 announcement that Energy21, Ecedo, Jules and Gridhub have become Eneve explains that the supplier's heritage billing package and its BRP's balancing platform now belong to one company with a consolidation roadmap. At an industry meeting the director of a comparable supplier describes running onboarding, billing, the customer portal and BRP as a Service on the same data model, and the reference logos on the vendor site are companies the COO competes with.

The vendor loads one of the supplier's brands from a heritage export and demonstrates a switch through EDSN, a billing run with guarantees of origin and split invoicing, a customer dispute in the portal and the resulting allocation and settlement view. The CFO checks the cost to serve business case against the licence, hosting and specialist cost of the heritage stack; the compliance officer reviews the market-change delivery record for 2025; two reference calls and a written migration plan with parallel run and support-until-decommission terms settle the decision.

The trial is a parallel run on the smallest brand of 40,000 connections: customers, connections, contracts, meter histories and open invoices are migrated, the next two billing runs and one month of allocation and settlement run in both systems, and invoices and volumes are compared line by line. Three mapping issues in guarantees-of-origin lines are fixed within a week and the controller signs off the first month close from the platform.

Within a year every brand and connection runs on the platform, the customer portal carries each brand, the third-party BRP contract is replaced by BRP as a Service, and the weekly operations meeting runs from the 15-minute margin dashboard. Two heritage contracts are terminated ahead of schedule and the proposition team launches a dynamic EV tariff in five weeks without an IT ticket.

Renewal is decided on numbers: cost to serve per connection is down by a third, the correction rate is below one percent and the 2026 market changes shipped without a project. The COO joins the customer advisory board, adds the Trade & Portfolio suite for the B2B desk and gives the reference call to the next supplier considering consolidation.

customerJourneyStories.name: A CFO buys balance responsibility as a service
customerJourneyStories.summary: The CFO of a growing supplier and producer portfolio operator of about 900 GWh a year, whose two-person balancing desk cannot keep up with 15-minute markets and aFRR changes, moves balance responsibility to BRP as a Service: triggered by a quarter of unexplained imbalance cost, discovering the managed service through the vendor's use-case pages and a trader's referral, evaluating on the guaranteed cycle and tiered MWh pricing, trialling on a bounded part of the portfolio, and staying because imbalance cost per MWh and 15-minute financial insight became a board metric.

stages.narrative: A volatile quarter produces imbalance cost twice the budget, the senior balancing specialist resigns and the 15-minute day-ahead market and the November 2025 aFRR changes are weeks away. The CFO decides that a two-person desk with a spreadsheet forecasting model is an uninsured risk, not a capability.

A trader at a partner company mentions that its portfolio is balanced by a managed BRP with a guaranteed cycle; the vendor's BRP as a Service page describes day-ahead, intraday and ex-post forecasting, TenneT nominations and re-nominations, ETPA intraday trading and up to 53% reduction in imbalance costs for portfolios from 40 GWh. The CFO recognises the vendor as the company behind the balancing platform its supplier already uses.

The vendor runs a back-test on twelve months of the portfolio's allocation data and shows what the guaranteed cycle would have cost and saved, per segment and per 15 minutes. The CFO compares tiered MWh pricing against the desk's fully loaded cost and the imbalance overrun, legal reviews the contract for balance responsibility and liability, and the risk committee checks that positions remain visible to the company in near real time. A reference from a wind and solar producer settles it.

The trial covers the solar production part of the portfolio for one quarter: forecasts, nominations and intraday steering run under the managed service while the desk keeps the rest, and imbalance cost per MWh is compared segment by segment every week. The first month shows the forecast error halving on sunny days and the CFO extends the trial to the supply portfolio.

Within six months the whole portfolio, including gas, is nominated and steered under BRP as a Service; the former desk specialists move into portfolio and pricing work; the 15-minute financial insight per segment becomes part of the monthly board pack and the basis for hedging decisions.

The service renews on a three-year term because imbalance cost per MWh is below the back-test, the aFRR and 15-minute market changes landed without the company noticing, and the vendor's quarterly review has become the CFO's window on the market. The company adds the Trade & Portfolio suite and asks the vendor to scope balance responsibility for its planned Belgian portfolio.

top.name: Gross margin per connection
top.description: Annual gross margin per household, business or industrial connection after sourcing, imbalance and grid pass-through cost, the director's headline measure of a healthy energy business.

branches.name: Margin and cost efficiency
branches.description: How much it costs to operate a connection and how much of the planned proposition margin is actually realised once sourcing and imbalance cost are in.

children.name: Cost to serve per connection
children.description: Fully loaded annual cost of onboarding, billing, collecting and serving a connection, including staff, systems and outsourced services.

children.name: Straight-through billing rate
children.description: Share of invoices produced by the billing run without manual intervention or subsequent correction.

children.name: Customer contact rate per connection
children.description: Calls, e-mails and chats per connection per year that reach an agent instead of being completed in the portal or app.

children.name: Proposition margin realisation
children.description: Share of the margin planned in a proposition's business case that is realised after actual sourcing, imbalance and operational cost.

children.name: Time to launch a new proposition
children.description: Weeks from approved proposition idea to first customer billed on it, across commercial, billing and market-communication setup.

children.name: Imbalance cost per MWh
children.description: Net imbalance settlement cost across the portfolio per MWh supplied or produced, the largest variable cost the director does not control directly.

branches.name: Compliance and operational control
branches.description: Whether the company is live on every market and regulatory change on time and how far the operation has been consolidated onto one platform.

children.name: Regulatory compliance incident rate
children.description: Regulator findings, TSO penalties, missed market-change go-lives and late regulatory reports per year across all brands and markets.

children.name: Market change readiness lead time
children.description: Days before the official go-live date that a market or regulatory change is implemented and parallel-run tested in production.

children.name: Regulatory report on-time rate
children.description: Share of ACM, CNMC, TenneT and BRP compliance reports submitted complete and on time.

children.name: Platform consolidation progress
children.description: Share of connections, portfolios and market roles running on the target platform rather than on heritage systems or outsourced services.

children.name: Heritage systems still in operation
children.description: Number of legacy billing, CRM, balancing and pricing systems still carrying live connections or portfolios.

children.name: Migration incidents per 100k connections
children.description: Customer-visible billing, market-message or nomination incidents caused by a migration wave, per 100,000 connections migrated.

top.name: Annual recurring revenue per energy company tenant
top.description: Average yearly subscription, module and managed-service revenue the platform earns per supplier, BRP or portfolio-operator tenant, scaling with connections and MWh.

branches.name: Suite expansion within the account
branches.description: How far each tenant expands beyond its heritage product into the other suites, the proposition builder, the portal and managed services.

children.name: Suites per tenant
children.description: Average number of the three suites (Supplier, Balancing & Shipping, Trade & Portfolio) a tenant runs on the platform.

children.name: Proposition builder attach rate
children.description: Share of supplier tenants with the low-code proposition builder live for their commercial team.

children.name: BRP as a Service attach rate
children.description: Share of tenants with a portfolio that have outsourced balance responsibility to the managed service.

children.name: Net revenue retention
children.description: Revenue from last year's tenants this year including connection growth, upsell and managed services, minus churn and downgrades.

children.name: Connections under subscription growth

children.name: Managed-service revenue share
children.description: Share of tenant revenue coming from BRP as a Service, market-entry and licensing projects and support rather than software subscriptions.

branches.name: Consolidation and retention
branches.description: How fast heritage-product customers are migrated onto the platform and how reliably tenants renew afterwards.

children.description: Tenants moved from Ecedo, EBASE, Jules, Gridhub or Nemon heritage products onto the consolidated platform per quarter.

children.name: Migration cost per 100k connections
children.description: Vendor implementation and tooling cost to migrate 100,000 connections from a heritage product to the platform.

children.name: Time to migrate a tenant
children.description: Months from signed migration plan to heritage system decommissioned for an average tenant.

children.name: Logo churn rate
children.description: Share of tenants that leave the platform in a year, including those lost in a customer's own acquisition.

children.name: Executive reference willingness

children.name: Subscription renewal rate

customers.name: New Market Entrant Lead
customers.description: Founder, country manager or expansion lead who is launching an energy supplier, a BRP or a producer portfolio in the Netherlands or Spain: a start-up building a dynamic-tariff or EV-first supplier, a Northern-European utility opening a Spanish retail business, a renewable developer that wants to sell its own production, a charge-point or heat-pump company adding energy supply, or an established supplier entering a second country. Owns the go or no-go decision and the launch budget, must obtain the ACM supply licence or the CNMC registration and market-agent status, contract or outsource balance responsibility, choose the operating model and stand up onboarding, billing, portal and market communication, usually with a small team and a board that expects first customers within a year. Judges the platform and its expertise services on time to first live customer, licensing lead time and setup cost per market, and on whether the launch team learns the market fast enough to avoid the mistakes that cost entrants six months.
careAbout: Time to first live customer: every month before revenue burns launch capital and tests the board's patience
A realistic licensing timeline for the ACM (8 to 14 weeks) or the CNMC (12 to 20 weeks) and a complete first submission rather than a six-month ramp of regulator questions
Choosing the right operating model early: which market roles to hold, what to outsource (BRP as a Service, billing operations) and what to build in-house
Setup cost per market: licence deposits and guarantees, staff hired before revenue, bespoke connectors and consultants must fit a launch budget
A commercial blueprint that differentiates, dynamic, EV, battery or green propositions priced against a portfolio the entrant does not yet have
Not underestimating market communication: EDSN, C-AR and TenneT in the Netherlands, SIPS, ATR, OMIE and distributor switching files in Spain must work before the first switch
winsThem: A market-entry scan that answers regulation, competition, operating model, commercial blueprint and roadmap in five weeks with a go or no-go the board can sign
Licensing support that gets the ACM or CNMC application complete the first time and keeps the timeline inside the published range
BRP as a Service and certified market-communication connectors that remove the need to hire balancing and market-messaging specialists before the first customer
A platform where the first propositions, onboarding flow, billing and portal are configured rather than built, with the team trained in the academy
A vendor that has taken other entrants live and knows which mistakes cost six months
theirFear: A licence application rejected or delayed by missing financial guarantees, governance evidence or an incomplete operating model
Going live and discovering that switches are rejected, bills are wrong or nominations are late in the first month with real customers
Running out of launch capital before the customer base is large enough to carry the fixed cost of market roles

jobsToBeDone.name: Decide whether and how to enter the market
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Turn an ambition to sell or balance energy in the Netherlands or Spain into a board-level go or no-go with a chosen segment, proposition, operating model, budget and timeline, based on a structured scan of regulation, competition, market economics and the roles the company will hold or outsource.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Within five weeks the board has a market-entry decision with an operating model, commercial blueprint, budget and roadmap it can sign, and the launch team knows which licences, market roles, partners and platform modules it needs and in what order.

steps.step: Frame the ambition and the segment
steps.description: Define whether the company wants to be a supplier, a BRP, a producer selling its own output or a combination, in which country, for which segment (households, SME, industrial, EV drivers, prosumers) and with what differentiation, so that the scan has a hypothesis to test rather than a market to describe.

streamsNeeded.name: Enter and Operate in a New Energy Market
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Structures the market-entry scan around the entrant's ambition, segment and country in the first of five workstreams.

steps.step: Run the regulatory and market-role scan
steps.description: Map the licences, registrations, financial guarantees, consumer-protection duties, market roles (supplier, BRP, metering responsible party, shipper) and market-communication obligations that apply in the Netherlands or Spain, and what each costs in time, deposits and staff.

streamsNeeded.name: Enter and Operate in a New Energy Market
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Delivers the regulatory scan workstream with ACM or CNMC requirements, timelines and guarantees.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate Market Communication and External Systems
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Lists the EDSN, C-AR, TenneT or SIPS, ATR and OMIE connections the entrant must certify before it can switch or nominate.

steps.step: Size competition, margins and sourcing cost
steps.description: Assess the competitive landscape, typical propositions and prices, switching behaviour, sourcing and imbalance cost for the target segment, and the gross margin per connection an entrant can realistically earn, so that the business case rests on market numbers rather than on the pitch deck.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides price curves, cost-plus pricing logic and margin models to test the entrant's proposition economics.

streamsNeeded.name: Launch Energy Propositions and Tariffs
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Shows which proposition types (fixed, variable, dynamic, EV, battery, bundled) competitors run and what the entrant can configure.

steps.step: Choose the operating model
steps.description: Decide which roles the company will hold itself and which it will outsource: balance responsibility in-house or as a service, billing and customer service in-house or with a partner, market communication through certified connectors, and the staffing this implies before and after go-live.

streamsNeeded.name: Enter and Operate in a New Energy Market
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Delivers the operating-model workstream with build, buy and outsource options and their cost and timeline.

streamsNeeded.name: Forecast and Nominate the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Shows what balance responsibility entails operationally so that the in-house versus BRP as a Service choice is informed.

steps.step: Build the commercial blueprint and roadmap
steps.description: Define the launch propositions, channels, pricing and customer journeys, the licensing and implementation timeline, the budget and the milestones to first customer and to break-even, and present a go or no-go to the board.

streamsNeeded.name: Launch Energy Propositions and Tariffs
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Turns the blueprint's propositions and channels into configurable products ready for the launch.

streamsNeeded.name: Enter and Operate in a New Energy Market
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Delivers the commercial blueprint and roadmap workstreams and the board-ready go or no-go.

jobsToBeDone.name: Obtain licences and market roles on a realistic timeline
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Secure the supply licence from the ACM or the CNMC registration and market-agent status, register the market roles and connections with EDSN, TenneT, the gas TSO, OMIE, REE and the distributors, pass the market-communication certification tests and contract balance responsibility and shipping, inside the published timelines and without a rejected or stalled application.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Licences and registrations are granted within 8 to 14 weeks (ACM) or 12 to 20 weeks (CNMC) from a complete first submission, market-communication tests pass, balance responsibility is contracted and the company is legally and technically able to take its first customer.

steps.step: Prepare a complete licence application
steps.description: Assemble the financial guarantees, governance and organisation evidence, operating model, consumer-protection policies and technical capability statements the ACM or CNMC requires, checked against the regulator's current checklist so that the first submission is complete.

streamsNeeded.name: Enter and Operate in a New Energy Market
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides licensing support with the regulator checklist, templates and review before submission.

steps.step: Register market roles and connections
steps.description: Register the company as a market participant with EDSN and the central connection register, with TenneT and the gas TSO for balance responsibility, or with OMIE, REE and the distributors in Spain, and set up the SIPS and ATR access needed for switching.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate Market Communication and External Systems
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the certified connectors and participant setup for each market-communication counterparty.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Sets up the allocation, reconciliation and settlement roles and reporting the entrant is bound to from day one.

steps.step: Pass market-communication certification tests
steps.description: Run the EDSN or distributor test scripts for switches, move-ins, meter data and master-data changes on the platform's connectors, fix any deviations and obtain the certification that allows production messaging.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate Market Communication and External Systems
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Runs the certification test scripts on connectors that are already certified for other tenants.

streamsNeeded.name: Collect and Validate Meter Data
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Validates the meter-data message flows that are part of the certification.

steps.step: Respond to regulator questions
steps.description: Answer the ACM or CNMC information requests fast and completely, with the expertise team translating regulatory language into the evidence the entrant can produce, so that the application does not stall.

streamsNeeded.name: Enter and Operate in a New Energy Market
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides licensing specialists who handle regulator correspondence and keep the timeline on track.

steps.step: Contract balance responsibility and shipping
steps.description: Sign the BRP contract with TenneT and the gas TSO or the BRP as a Service agreement, agree the portfolio, EAN types and MWh pricing, and set up the nomination and settlement relationship so that the first customer's volume is balanced from the first day.

streamsNeeded.name: Forecast and Nominate the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Sets up forecasting and nomination for the new portfolio, in-house or under the managed service.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Establishes imbalance settlement and BRP compliance reporting for the entrant's portfolio.

jobsToBeDone.name: Go live with customers and balance responsibility in months
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Stand up the propositions, onboarding, billing, payments, portal, market communication and balancing the entrant needs, train the launch team and take the first customers live with correct switches, bills and nominations, within months of the licence rather than after a year of building.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: The first customer is switched, billed and balanced within months of licensing; the launch team runs onboarding, billing and service on the platform without specialists it could not hire; the first-year correction and rejection rates are those of an established supplier.

steps.step: Configure the launch propositions
steps.description: Set up the launch products, tariffs, pricing logic, journeys and channels in the proposition builder from the commercial blueprint, including dynamic or EV tariffs that depend on 15-minute prices, so that they are billable from day one.

streamsNeeded.name: Launch Energy Propositions and Tariffs
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Configures the launch propositions and channels and plugs them into billing automatically.

steps.step: Set up onboarding, billing and payments
steps.description: Configure intake, identity and credit check, contract creation, the switch and move-in processes, billing cycles, VAT, guarantees of origin, direct debit and dunning for the target segment, using the platform's standard flows rather than building them.

streamsNeeded.name: Onboard and Switch Customers
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the standard intake, credit-check and switching flows the entrant configures per channel.

streamsNeeded.name: Bill and Reconcile Customers
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides configured billing runs, VAT and settlement logic for the chosen propositions.

streamsNeeded.name: Collect Payments and Manage Debtors
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Sets up direct debit, payment matching and dunning with the entrant's payment provider.

steps.step: Launch the branded portal and app
steps.description: Configure the white-label portal and app with the entrant's brand so that customers see invoices, consumption and their contract and can submit readings, change tariffs and raise requests from the first day, without a service team sized for the calls a supplier without a portal gets.

streamsNeeded.name: Serve Customers Through Portal and Care
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the branded portal, app and case management on the same data as billing.

steps.step: Onboard the portfolio to balancing
steps.description: Load the expected portfolio and EAN types, start day-ahead, intraday and ex-post forecasting and nominations under BRP as a Service or in-house, and rehearse the guaranteed cycle before the first customer's volume is allocated.

streamsNeeded.name: Forecast and Nominate the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Starts forecasting and nominations for the entrant's portfolio from the first connection.

streamsNeeded.name: Steer Intraday and Optimise Imbalance
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Runs intraday steering and the ETPA cycle so that a small, volatile launch portfolio does not generate outsized imbalance cost.

steps.step: Train the launch team
steps.description: Put the founders, billing, service and balancing staff through the academy on the market processes, the platform workflows and the exception handling they will meet, so that the first weeks with real customers are run by a team that knows the Dutch or Spanish market rules.

streamsNeeded.name: Enter and Operate in a New Energy Market
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Delivers academy training and implementation support tailored to the entrant's operating model.

steps.step: Take the first customers live and monitor
steps.description: Switch the first cohort of customers, watch switch acceptance, meter-data arrival, first invoices, payments and nominations daily on the operational dashboard, and fix the first exceptions with the vendor's support before scaling acquisition.

streamsNeeded.name: Onboard and Switch Customers
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Processes the first switches and move-ins and shows rejections and their causes immediately.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Confirms that the first customers' volumes are allocated, nominated and settled correctly.

customerJourneyStories.name: A Dutch founder launches a dynamic-tariff supplier in nine months
customerJourneyStories.summary: The founder of a start-up that wants to sell 15-minute dynamic and EV tariffs to prosumers adopts the platform and its expertise services: triggered by the 15-minute day-ahead market and the net-metering phase-out, discovering the vendor through an ACM licence list and an investor, evaluating the market-entry scan and BRP as a Service against building a team, trialling with the five-week scan and a licensing engagement, and staying because the first customers went live within months and the platform kept pace with growth.

stages.narrative: The move of the Dutch day-ahead market to 15-minute blocks and the announced 2027 phase-out of net metering convince the founder that prosumers with solar, batteries and EVs will need a supplier that prices per quarter hour. The seed round is closed on the promise of first customers within a year, and the founder has no licence, no BRP and no billing system.

Scanning the ACM list of licensed suppliers, the founder notices that several recent entrants run on the same platform; an investor who backed one of them names the vendor and its market-entry scan. The vendor's site describes five workstreams in five weeks, ACM licensing support of 8 to 14 weeks and the warning that most entrants underestimate the licensing ramp by six months or more, which matches what the founder has heard.

The founder compares the scan plus platform plus BRP as a Service route against hiring a balancing specialist, a billing developer and a market-communication consultant. A reference call with an entrant that went live the year before, a sample scan report, the tiered MWh pricing from 40 GWh and the fact that the platform's connectors are already certified with EDSN settle it; the board approves the scan as the first spend.

The five-week scan delivers the regulatory checklist, the competitive overview of dynamic-tariff suppliers, an operating model with BRP as a Service and outsourced payment collection, a commercial blueprint with three launch propositions and a roadmap. The go decision follows, and the licensing engagement starts with a complete ACM submission in the sixth week.

While the ACM processes the application, the launch team configures the propositions, onboarding, billing and the branded app, passes the EDSN certification tests on the platform's connectors and trains in the academy. The licence arrives in week twelve; the first two hundred customers are switched, billed and balanced under the managed BRP in month nine.

A year after go-live the supplier has 20,000 connections, a correction rate below two percent and imbalance cost in line with the back-test; the platform subscription and MWh pricing scale with the base rather than with headcount. The founder speaks at the vendor's academy day and commissions a Belgian market-entry scan on the same platform.

customerJourneyStories.name: A Northern-European utility opens a Spanish retail business
customerJourneyStories.summary: The expansion lead of a Dutch utility that wants to sell electricity to SMEs in Spain adopts the Iberian supplier platform and licensing services: triggered by a board mandate to grow outside the home market, discovering the vendor's Spanish capability through the Nemon acquisition, evaluating the CNMC timeline and the SIPS and ATR market communication against a local acquisition, trialling with a dual-market scan, and staying because one platform now runs both countries.

stages.narrative: The board asks for a second country within two years and Spain's SME segment, where about a hundred suppliers compete and solar production is growing, comes out top of the internal screening. The expansion lead knows the Dutch platform well but nothing about CNMC registration, SIPS, ATR access or OMIE.

The March 2026 news that the utility's Dutch platform vendor has acquired Nemon, with about a hundred supplier customers in Spain and Portugal, reaches the expansion lead through the vendor's account manager and an industry newsletter. The vendor's dual-market entry scan and the 16 to 20 week combined licensing timeline are exactly the questions on the expansion lead's desk.

The expansion lead compares a greenfield entry on the Iberian platform with buying a small Spanish supplier and its systems. The vendor presents Nemon's Trade Energy, CRM and SIPS modules with references from Spanish suppliers, a CNMC registration plan of 12 to 20 weeks and a cross-border operating model in which the Dutch portfolio desk prices the Spanish book. Legal checks the guarantees, finance the setup cost per market, and the group CIO the fact that both countries will report into one data model.

The trial is the five-week dual-market scan with the Spanish regulatory workstream, a competitive overview of the SME segment, the operating model and a blueprint of three cost-plus propositions. The scan surfaces a guarantee requirement the utility had not budgeted and a distributor switching-file process that needs SIPS access from week one; both go into the plan before the go decision.

The CNMC registration is granted in week sixteen; the Spanish operation goes live on the Iberian platform with OMIE and REE connections, SIPS switching and a Spanish-language portal, while Dutch pricing and risk teams see the Spanish positions in the same dashboards. The first thousand SME sites are supplied within a year.

The Spanish business renews and expands to Portugal on the same platform because setup cost per market came in under budget and the two-country operation needs no second back office. The expansion lead becomes the group's reference for the vendor's Iberian roadmap and asks for a German scan next.

customers.name: Household or Business Energy Customer
customers.description: A household, small business or multi-site SME supplied by one of the platform's supplier tenants in the Netherlands, Belgium, Spain or Portugal: one of the 7 million households and 3 million business customers served by Dutch supplier clients, or a Spanish SME supplied through a Nemon-based supplier. Signs up or switches through a comparison site, a sales channel or the supplier's own site, moves house, receives monthly advances and an annual settlement or monthly actual-usage bills, and increasingly has solar panels, a heat pump, an EV or a home battery on a dynamic or time-of-use contract. Uses the supplier's white-label portal and app for free to see invoices and consumption, submit meter readings, change tariff, advance or payment method, raise a dispute or a service request, and expects the bill to be right and the answer to be available without calling. Judges the supplier, and indirectly the platform, on bill accuracy, ease of self-service and how fast a switch, move-in or dispute is handled.
careAbout: A correct bill: advances that match actual consumption, an annual settlement without a shock and invoice lines that can be checked against the meter
Seeing what energy is used and what it costs per day, hour or quarter hour, especially on a dynamic contract, with solar feed-in shown correctly as net metering is phased out
Switching or moving in on the requested date without a rejected switch, a double bill or a gap in supply
Doing things themselves in the app at any hour: readings, tariff and advance changes, payment method, moving, a question, a complaint
Fair treatment when money is tight: a payment plan, a warning before dunning, no disconnection without contact
Trust that the supplier follows the rules on tariffs, contract terms, notice periods and price changes
winsThem: An app that shows consumption, cost and the next invoice on the same numbers the supplier bills from, so what the customer sees is what they pay
A switch or move-in confirmed with a date and a welcome that lists exactly what happens next
Meter readings, tariff changes and payment arrangements that take two minutes and need no call or letter
A dispute that can be raised in the app with the invoice attached and answered by someone who sees the same data
Propositions that fit the household: dynamic pricing, EV charging tariffs, battery and solar bundles offered when they make sense
theirFear: An annual settlement demanding hundreds of euros because advances were set on an estimate nobody corrected
A switch or move that goes wrong and leaves them with two suppliers, a rejected request or no supply on moving day
Being stuck in a call queue or an e-mail loop about a wrong bill while a direct debit keeps running

jobsToBeDone.name: Switch or move in without hassle
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Become a customer of a new supplier, or take supply at a new address, with a clear offer, a short sign-up, a switch or move-in processed correctly through the market on the requested date, a correct opening reading and a welcome that explains the advance and what happens next.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Supply starts on the requested date without a rejected request, double billing or a gap; the first advance is realistic; the customer knows what they signed and has a working portal account before the first invoice.

steps.description: Compare fixed, variable, dynamic and EV or solar propositions on a comparison site, the supplier's site or through a sales partner, see the tariff, terms and expected annual cost for the household's usage, and pick one without hidden conditions.

streamsNeeded.name: Onboard and Switch Customers
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Runs intake, identity and credit check and contract creation from the sign-up in one flow.

streamsNeeded.name: Collect Payments and Manage Debtors
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Sets up the direct debit mandate or chosen payment method at sign-up.

steps.step: Have the switch or move-in processed on the requested date

streamsNeeded.name: Onboard and Switch Customers
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Submits and tracks the switch or move-in market process and confirms the date to the customer.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate Market Communication and External Systems

streamsNeeded.name: Serve Customers Through Portal and Care

steps.step: Get a welcome, a realistic advance and a portal account
steps.description: Receive a welcome with the contract, the first advance based on the household's expected usage, the direct debit dates and an invitation to the portal and app, so that the customer is set up before the first invoice arrives.

streamsNeeded.name: Serve Customers Through Portal and Care
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Sends the welcome communication and activates the portal account on the new contract.

streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Calculates the first advance from expected consumption and the contracted tariff.

jobsToBeDone.name: Understand and trust my bill and consumption
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: See what energy the household or business uses and what it costs, check each invoice line against the meter and the tariff, avoid a surprise at the annual settlement by adjusting the advance in time, and get a wrong bill corrected quickly when it happens.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: The customer can explain every invoice to themselves, the annual settlement is within an expected range, disputes are rare and resolved in days, and the customer trusts the supplier enough to stay.

steps.step: See consumption and cost per day, hour or quarter hour
steps.description: Look at electricity and gas consumption, solar feed-in and cost over time in the app, including per-quarter-hour prices on a dynamic contract, so that the effect of an EV, a heat pump or a cold week is visible before the invoice.

streamsNeeded.name: Collect and Validate Meter Data
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides validated interval consumption and feed-in data per connection.

streamsNeeded.name: Serve Customers Through Portal and Care
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Shows consumption history, cost and projected annual cost in the portal and app.

steps.step: Read the invoice breakdown
steps.description: Open the invoice in the app and see supply, grid, taxes, VAT, guarantees of origin and feed-in credit as separate lines with the readings and tariff behind each, so that the amount is checkable rather than a black box.

streamsNeeded.name: Bill and Reconcile Customers
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Produces the invoice with a line-level breakdown from validated volumes and the contracted tariff.

streamsNeeded.name: Serve Customers Through Portal and Care
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Presents the invoice breakdown and the readings behind it in the app.

steps.step: Check the projected annual cost and adjust the advance
steps.description: See the projected annual cost and the expected settlement based on actual consumption to date, and raise or lower the monthly advance in the app so that the annual settlement stays small.

streamsNeeded.name: Serve Customers Through Portal and Care
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Shows the projection and lets the customer change the advance within the supplier's rules.

streamsNeeded.name: Bill and Reconcile Customers
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Recalculates the projection and applies the new advance to the next billing cycle.

steps.step: Handle the annual settlement

streamsNeeded.name: Collect Payments and Manage Debtors

steps.description: Raise a dispute in the app on the specific invoice with the reason and evidence, have the direct debit for the disputed amount paused, and get a corrected invoice or an explanation from someone who sees the same readings and tariff.

jobsToBeDone.name: Manage my contract, payments and requests myself
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Change tariff, contract type, advance, payment method or contact details, submit readings, manage smart-meter data consent, add solar, a battery or an EV to the contract, and move out or end the contract, all in the portal or app at any time, without calling or writing.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Routine changes and requests are completed in the app in minutes with immediate confirmation; the customer only contacts the supplier for things that need a person; the contract keeps fitting the household as it changes.

steps.step: Change tariff or contract type
steps.description: Switch from variable to fixed, to a dynamic quarter-hour contract or to an EV or time-of-use tariff, see the effect on expected cost before confirming, and have the change applied from the next billing period without a new sign-up.

steps.step: Change advance, payment method or bank account
steps.description: Adjust the monthly advance, switch between direct debit and transfer, change the bank account or the collection date, or set up a payment plan, with the change effective from the next collection.

streamsNeeded.name: Collect Payments and Manage Debtors
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Updates the mandate, payment method, collection date or payment plan and applies it to the next run.

steps.step: Submit readings and manage smart-meter data consent

streamsNeeded.name: Collect and Validate Meter Data
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Accepts customer readings, validates them and applies the consent to smart-meter data collection.

streamsNeeded.name: Serve Customers Through Portal and Care

customerJourneyStories.name: A household switches to a dynamic contract and stays for the app
customerJourneyStories.summary: A family with solar panels and a new EV in Utrecht switches to a supplier on the platform for a dynamic quarter-hour tariff and adopts the supplier's white-label app: triggered by an annual settlement shock and the coming net-metering phase-out, discovering the supplier through a comparison site and a neighbour's app, evaluating on transparent quarter-hour pricing and reviews, trialling with the switch and the first month of consumption insight, and staying because the app makes the bill understandable.

stages.narrative: The annual settlement from the current supplier asks for EUR 480 because the advance was set before the EV arrived, and a news item explains that net metering for solar will end in 2027. The family wants a contract where the EV charges when electricity is cheap and the solar feed-in is visible, and a supplier whose bill they can check.

A comparison site lists several dynamic-tariff suppliers; a neighbour shows the app of one of them with quarter-hour prices, charging cost per session and feed-in per day. The family recognises the supplier from an EV forum where members praise the fact that the app shows the same numbers as the invoice.

The family compares the dynamic tariff against a fixed contract with an EV add-on, reads the terms on price components, notice period and how the advance is set, checks reviews on switching problems and consumer-organisation ratings, and confirms that the app supports readings, disputes and payment changes. The transparent breakdown and the fact that the switch date is guaranteed decide it.

The sign-up takes five minutes; the switch is confirmed for the first of the month and the app is active before supply starts. In the first month the family checks daily consumption, sets the EV to charge in the cheap night hours and sees the projected annual cost fall; the first invoice matches what the app predicted to the euro.

The app becomes a weekly habit: the family watches feed-in in summer, adjusts the advance before winter, submits a reading when the smart meter has a gap and raises one dispute about a grid-charge line that is answered with the reading in two days. No call is ever made.

When a competitor offers a cheaper fixed contract the family stays: the annual settlement is a small refund, the bill is understandable and the supplier has just offered a battery bundle in the app for the post-net-metering years. They recommend the supplier on the EV forum that brought them.

customerJourneyStories.name: A small business with three sites moves onto the supplier's portal
customerJourneyStories.summary: The owner of a bakery with three shops in Rotterdam, supplied under one business contract, adopts the supplier's business portal: triggered by three separate paper invoices a month and a dispute nobody could trace, discovering the portal through the supplier's account manager and an invoice footer, evaluating on split invoicing and per-site insight, trialling with one site's history, and staying because the accountant now downloads everything and the bill is right.

stages.narrative: Every month three paper invoices arrive for three shops, one of them regularly on an estimated reading, and a disputed invoice from the spring has gone back and forth by e-mail for eight weeks while the direct debit kept running. The owner wants one place to see what each shop uses and pays.

The supplier's account manager mentions during the contract renewal that the business portal shows all sites, invoices and readings in one login and that the supplier moved to a new platform last year; the invoice footer and a renewal e-mail carry the same invitation. The owner's accountant has seen the portal at another client.

The owner looks at whether the portal shows consumption per shop, whether invoices can be split per site and downloaded for the accountant, whether readings can be submitted with a photo when a meter is not read remotely, and whether a dispute can be raised on a specific invoice. A short demo by the account manager and the supplier's promise that the portal data is the billing data settle it.

The owner activates the portal, adds the accountant as a user and starts with one shop: twelve months of readings and invoices are there, the estimated reading is replaced by a submitted one with a photo and a corrected invoice appears within a week. The spring dispute is re-raised in the portal and closed in four days.

All three shops are managed in the portal, invoices are split per site and pulled by the accountant monthly, the advance for the busiest shop is raised before the winter and the owner checks weekly consumption after installing a new oven. Contact with the supplier drops to one question a year.

At the next renewal the owner accepts the supplier's offer with a rooftop solar feed-in proposition for the largest shop, chosen in the portal, rather than tendering the contract. Bill accuracy and the accountant's time saved outweigh the small price difference a competitor offers.

productStrategy.vision: Give every household and business supplied through the platform a bill that is right and understandable and a portal and app on the same data as billing and settlement, so that switching, moving, reading, paying, changing and disputing happen in minutes without a call and customers stay because the supplier is easy to trust.

year1.focus: Make the white-label portal and app a standard attach for every supplier tenant with invoice breakdown, consumption history, projected cost, readings, tariff and payment changes and disputes on the billing data; cut estimated readings and settlement shocks through validated smart-meter data and advance projections; and support dynamic quarter-hour contracts and feed-in display ahead of the net-metering phase-out.
year1.productTheme: One portal on the billing data: correct bills and self-service for every tenant's customers

supporting: Time to switch or move in

revenueStreams: Portal and app module subscriptions per supplier tenant scaled by connections
Customer-service case management and communication modules
Dynamic-contract and proposition modules enabled through the portal

milestones: Ship the white-label portal and app with invoice breakdown, projected annual cost, advance adjustment and dispute cases to every supplier tenant
Show quarter-hour prices, consumption and feed-in for dynamic contracts in the app for the 15-minute market
Bring the estimated-reading share of invoiced volume below five percent on tenants with smart-meter consent flows

year3.focus: Turn the portal into the customer's energy cockpit: EV, battery and solar assets registered and shown per device, proposition offers and retention propositions surfaced in context, payment plans and dunning prevention in the app, multi-site business views with split invoicing, and the same experience for Spanish and Portuguese customers on the Iberian platform.
year3.productTheme: The customer's energy cockpit for households, prosumers and multi-site businesses

supporting: Portal and app active users share

revenueStreams: Portal, app and asset-registration modules
In-app proposition and retention offer modules
Business portal and split-invoicing modules

milestones: Register EV, battery and solar assets per connection and show charging, storage and feed-in separately in the app
Surface eligible propositions and retention offers in the portal with one-tap acceptance for every tenant
Launch the multi-site business portal with split invoicing on the Dutch and Iberian platforms

year5.focus: Let customers hand routine energy decisions to the app: AI-assisted answers to bill questions grounded in the customer's own readings and tariff, automatic advance tuning, steering of EV charging and batteries against quarter-hour prices with the customer's consent, and proactive alerts before a settlement, a dunning step or a contract end.
year5.productTheme: Self-driving energy self-service with the customer in control

revenueStreams: AI-assisted customer-service and self-service modules
Flexibility steering modules for EV and battery propositions
Multi-country portal subscriptions

milestones: Answer the majority of bill questions in the app with AI assistance grounded in the customer's readings and tariff, under supplier supervision
Tune advances automatically from consumption and price projections for consenting customers
Steer EV charging and home batteries against quarter-hour prices for customers on flexibility propositions across the platform's countries
